verdict: FAIL — the shared predicate and the incident lane are genuinely well built and well tested (37/37 new assertions pass, strong discriminating negative controls), but PRD acceptance criterion AC-5 / FR-3 ('all four dispatch lanes consult the shared predicate — an in-flight item is withheld by EVERY lane') is NOT met: 2 of the 4 lanes are structurally inert in production because no caller ever supplies the input they read. The lane-2 tests pass only because the test itself constructs the ctx field that production never builds — stubbed-writer blindness (PAT-TEST-STUBBED-WRITER-UNVERIFIED-001) over a writer-consumer asymmetry (PAT-LEO-INFRA-WRITER-CONSUMER-ASYMMETRY-001). Path to PASS is small and concrete: wire the two missing producers and add the TS-12 parity tests.
summary: Ran npx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/fleet/ tests/unit/claim-eligibility.test.js: 1294 passed / 3 failed (1297 total, 99 files, 97 passed). The 3 failures are in spawn-control.test.js (1) and cp3-restart-relaunch-live-flag-propagation.test.js (2). PRE-EXISTING CLAIM INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AND TRUE: a clean detached worktree at merge-base 176446d3ad9 (node_modules junctioned, no branch code present) reproduces exactly the same 3 failures, 3 failed / 66 passed. The three new files pass 37/37. Independent verification found four substantive issues: (1) lib/fleet/claim-eligibility.cjs inflightGitAxes reads ctx.inflight_git_state and NO production caller supplies it — all 16 call sites of classifyDispatchIneligibility pass a ctx without that key, so the axis can never fire outside the test; (2) scripts/modules/sd-next/display/quick-fixes.js reads sessionContext.inFlightQfIds and no caller supplies it either (the lib/quality/assist-engine.js:233 occurrence is an unrelated local variable in a different module that is never passed to classifyQuickFixes), and that lane has zero tests of any kind; (3) both lane-1 and lane-3 derive the gh --repo from list[0].target_application only, while the live QF population is heterogeneous (EHG_Engineer 91, EHG 2, apexniche-ai 1 across 94 non-terminal QFs), so a mixed batch probes the wrong repo for the remainder — the exact wrong-repo false negative FR-7/TS-10 exists to prevent; (4) two tests make real unseeded gh/git network calls (critical-qf-jump-inflight.test.js:84-85 at 1569ms, and the new code path inside the PRE-EXISTING worker-checkin-qf-candidate-query-retry.test.js at 869ms), contradicting the test file's own 'no network, no gh auth' docblock. The PR-authoritative default change is sound in direction and all four ACs do still hold under it, and the opt-in path is covered in all three test files.
findings: VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING: merge-base 176446d3ad9 run in a clean detached worktree reproduces 3 failed / 66 passed on tests/unit/fleet/spawn-control.test.js ('FR-6 restarting a profile-stamped session with NO profiles dir configured FAILS LOUD') and tests/unit/fleet/cp3-restart-relaunch-live-flag-propagation.test.js (2 canaryRestart/canaryRelaunchUnderProfile opts.live cases). Identical failure set on the branch. The claim holds — these are unrelated to this SD, which touches none of those modules.

BLOCKER — LANE 2 INERT: lib/fleet/claim-eligibility.cjs:402 gates the whole axis on `if (!(ctx && ctx.inflight_git_state)) return null;`. grep across all .cjs/.js/.mjs shows the ONLY writers of inflight_git_state are tests/unit/fleet/claim-eligibility-inflight-axis.test.js. All 16 production call sites (belt-depth.cjs:60, merged-pool-self-claim.cjs:193, coordinator/dispatch.cjs:266, directed-assignment.cjs:104, tier-claimable.cjs:57/79/82/121, worker-checkin.cjs:955/1186, coordinator-backlog-rank.mjs:97, coordinator-capacity-forecast.mjs:289, stale-session-sweep.cjs:2641) pass ctx without it. The SD axis withholds nothing in production today.

BLOCKER — LANE 4 INERT AND UNTESTED: scripts/modules/sd-next/display/quick-fixes.js:176 reads `sessionContext.inFlightQfIds instanceof Set ? ... : new Set()`. No caller sets it — the three real callers (fallback-queue.js:66, fallback-queue.js:109, SDNextSelector.js:905 via this.getSessionContext()) pass session contexts without that key, so inFlightIds is permanently the empty Set and the added `&& !inFlightIds.has(qf.id)` clause in topStartableQF is a no-op. Additionally NO test anywhere references inFlightQfIds or _inFlight for this module, so the lane has zero coverage in either direction.

Both inert lanes are consumers with no producer. The code comments acknowledge the design ('The snapshot is precomputed by the caller', 'The caller passes an already-computed id Set') but the producer was never implemented. This is the same writer-consumer asymmetry class the SD family exists to close, and the lane-2 tests give false green because they construct the ctx production never builds.

LANE COVERAGE MATRIX: (1) lib/checkin/steps/critical-qf-jump.cjs — LIVE and WELL TESTED (10 assertions, real probe via withheldFilteredQfs with resolved repo). (2) lib/fleet/claim-eligibility.cjs — INERT in production; 7 assertions all against a test-constructed ctx. (3) scripts/worker-checkin.cjs:667 — LIVE (calls withheldFilteredQfs(sorted, {})) but NO direct test of this call site; it inherits coverage only via the shared helper. (4) scripts/modules/sd-next/display/quick-fixes.js — INERT and completely untested. So 2 of 4 lanes cannot withhold, and 2 of 4 lanes (3 and 4) have no lane-level test.

TS-12 ('FR-6 parity for the three QF lanes, not just the SD axis') is NOT COVERED. The only with/without-input parity assertions are in claim-eligibility-inflight-axis.test.js, which is the SD axis — precisely the one lane TS-12 says is already covered. Neither worker-checkin's self-claim loop nor quick-fixes.js has a with-input/without-input pair.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS — STRONG: TS-3 unauth gh asserts reason===gh_exit_nonzero AND runGh called exactly once, which correctly discriminates the clean exit-4 path from the ENOENT that the unit project's pinned FLEET_REPO_ROOT would otherwise produce; a bare 'UNAVAILABLE' assertion would have been vacuous. TS-3 timeout asserts reason==='timeout' distinctly. TS-8 asserts parse_error and explicitly `not.toBe(CLEAR)`. critical-qf-jump-inflight.test.js is the best test in the set: every fixture pins pr_url AND commit_sha NULL, which is the exact shape the pre-existing column guard (.is('pr_url',null).is('commit_sha',null) / isAutoStartableQF's `if (qf.pr_url || qf.commit_sha) return false`) cannot catch, so a withhold there is attributable to the new probe and nothing else. All of it would fail against pre-fix code (withheldFilteredQfs did not exist).

NEGATIVE CONTROLS — ASSERTIONS THAT WOULD PASS WITH THE FEATURE ABSENT (named as requested; valid as regression controls, but they are NOT feature evidence): claim-eligibility-inflight-axis.test.js:52-55 'AC-4 regression: an SD with no branch and no PR stays claimable' (pre-fix returns null → passes); :63-68 'no ctx at all: identical to before the axis existed' (passes trivially pre-fix); :70-74 'ctx present but without inflight_git_state: still a no-op' (passes trivially pre-fix); :85-88 'a malformed snapshot object does not throw or block' (passes pre-fix); and the classify half of :78-83 'unauthenticated gh leaves every row claimable' — its only non-vacuous content is `expect(snap.status).toBe('UNAVAILABLE')`, since the classify call returns null pre-fix too. Also weak-by-construction: inflight-git-state.test.js:91 `expect(classifyItem.length).toBe(2)` is an arity proxy for 'does not read DB columns', not a behavioural assertion; and TS-10's 'verdict identical from two cwds' is vacuous under an injected seam (a fake runner cannot vary by cwd) — the load-bearing part of that test is the --repo argv capture at :198-199.

DEFAULT CHANGE (a) REASONING SOUND, WITH ONE UNPARTITIONED PREMISE: the direction is right and evidence-based — this repo squash-merges without pruning (3059 refs), audit-unrouted-branches.mjs exists for that reason, and QF-20260727-703's ref survived its own merge. A false withhold blocks an item indefinitely and presents as an empty queue, which is worse than one wasted duplicate build. BUT the measured '6 of 24 branch-only' was never partitioned into stale-merged refs vs genuinely-active WIP-without-a-PR. Those 6 are the evidence for dropping the signal, and only the first subset justifies it. The branch-only signal is the ONLY signal covering the push→open-PR window, which is exactly the correction-delivery window this SD is about. The right long-term fix is branch freshness (exclude refs already merged into main via commit ancestry / committerdate), not discarding the disjunct.

DEFAULT CHANGE (b) ALL FOUR ACs GENUINELY STILL HOLD: AC-1 and AC-2 both stage a remote branch AND an open PR, so the PR signal alone satisfies them and both are exercised by real assertions. AC-3 is orthogonal to which signal counts. AC-4 is neither branch nor PR and is unaffected. No AC is left untested by the default flip — the author's claim is correct. What IS newly untested-by-default is the SD's branch-only disjunct, which now only runs under opt-in.

DEFAULT CHANGE (c) OPT-IN IS COVERED — three places assert includeBranchOnly:true yields IN_FLIGHT with reason inflight_remote_branch: inflight-git-state.test.js:80-83, critical-qf-jump-inflight.test.js:54-58, claim-eligibility-inflight-axis.test.js:48-49. However NO production caller ever passes includeBranchOnly, so the branch-only path is dead code in the shipped configuration.

COUPLING DEFECT: collectInflightSnapshot returns UNAVAILABLE if `git ls-remote` fails (lines 168-176), even though under the shipped default the resulting branchRefs are discarded and never consulted (line 202-204 only unions them when includeBranchOnly is true). So a git/network failure disables the PR-based guard whose answer does not depend on git at all, needlessly raising the inert-guard rate. inflight-git-state.test.js:134-139 ('a failing git half does not serve a half-snapshot as CLEAR') cements this behaviour rather than flagging it. Under the default the git probe could be skipped entirely, which would also halve the per-tick cost.

WRONG-REPO RISK, UNGUARDED AND UNTESTED: both critical-qf-jump.cjs:22 and the worker-checkin lane derive the repo from `list[0]?.target_application` — one repo for the entire batch. Measured live: 94 non-terminal quick-fixes span EHG_Engineer (91), EHG (2) and apexniche-ai (1), so a heterogeneous candidate list probes the wrong repository for every element after the first and returns a false CLEAR. That is precisely the failure mode TR-6/FR-7 rate as the most dangerous ('a wrong-repo probe returns nothing-in-flight and silently re-opens the defect while appearing to work'). TS-10 guards that --repo is passed, not that it is the RIGHT repo per item. Today's critical+open slice happens to be 9/9 EHG_Engineer so the incident lane is currently safe by luck; the broader worker-checkin lane is not.

FLAKINESS — REAL NETWORK I/O IN THE UNIT TIER: critical-qf-jump-inflight.test.js:83-86 passes ctx `{}`, so no seam is injected and filterOutInFlight runs the DEFAULT runners — a live `gh pr list --repo rickfelix/EHG_Engineer` plus a live `git ls-remote --heads origin`. Measured 1569ms against ~2ms for every other test in the file. Note filterOutInFlight probes BEFORE iterating, so even an empty candidate list triggers it. This contradicts the file's own docblock ('no network, no gh auth, no real repo'). Worst case is 2x PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 8s per cold cache under a network partition.

FLAKINESS — NETWORK INTRODUCED INTO A PRE-EXISTING TEST: the new `await withheldFilteredQfs(sortQfCandidatesBySeverity(qfs), {})` in scripts/worker-checkin.cjs:672 has no seam, so tests/unit/worker-checkin-qf-candidate-query-retry.test.js (which existed before this branch) now makes a live gh/git call — measured 869ms on its first case vs 2ms on the second (module-level TTL cache warm, and that file never calls _resetSnapshotCache). The verdict of a pre-existing unit test now depends on live GitHub state.

FLAKINESS — CLEAN AREAS: no hardcoded date comparison anywhere (QF-20260726-425 / SD-LEO-INFRA-* are opaque string ids, never parsed or compared to a clock), so the failure mode that quarantined tests/unit/worker-checkin-critical-qf-priority-jump.test.js is NOT reproduced. The TTL tests correctly inject `now` (inflight-git-state.test.js:165-188) rather than relying on Date.now or timers. Cache isolation is handled via _resetSnapshotCache in beforeEach in the two files that use the cache; claim-eligibility-inflight-axis.test.js calls collectInflightSnapshot directly and bypasses the cache, so its omission of the reset is safe.

TR-5 SATISFIED: all three new files are .test.js under tests/unit/fleet/, none is .test.mjs, and none of the assertions were added to the quarantined tests/unit/worker-checkin-critical-qf-priority-jump.test.js. Confirmed all 37 assertions actually execute under `--project unit` (verbose run enumerated every one).

TR-6 SATISFIED: every fail-open verdict carries a discriminating token (REASON.GH_EXIT_NONZERO / GIT_EXIT_NONZERO / SPAWN_ERROR / PARSE_ERROR / NO_SNAPSHOT / 'timeout'), and the SR-1 security property of the DEFAULT runner is asserted outside the seam via a source-text scan (inflight-git-state.test.js:206-233) that correctly strips comments first so the docblock quoting `shell: process.platform === 'win32'` does not self-match. That comment-stripping detail is a genuinely good catch by the author.

TS-9 (dual CJS/ESM) COVERED and correctly asserts EQUIVALENCE rather than identity (inflight-git-state.test.js:250-263), which is the property TR-1 actually needs given vitest can hand require() and import() distinct instances. TS-10 (explicit --repo) COVERED for the argv assertion. TS-11 (TTL expiry) COVERED properly with an injected clock plus repo-keyed cache isolation. TS-12 (QF-lane ctx parity) NOT COVERED.
required_additions: BLOCKER 1 — Wire a producer for ctx.inflight_git_state. Compute the snapshot once per tick via getInflightSnapshot() at the dispatch entry points that classify SD rows (at minimum lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs:266 and lib/checkin/steps/merged-pool-self-claim.cjs:193) and pass it through in ctx. Leave the DB-free callers (belt-depth.cjs:60, coordinator-backlog-rank.mjs:97, stale-session-sweep.cjs:2641) unchanged so FR-6 purity holds. Without this, lane 2 withholds nothing in production.

BLOCKER 2 — Wire a producer for sessionContext.inFlightQfIds. Populate it in the sd:next session-context builder(s) feeding classifyQuickFixes (SDNextSelector.getSessionContext() and the fallback-queue.js path), deriving the Set from filterOutInFlight over the open QF list. Without this, the topStartableQF guard is a permanent no-op.

BLOCKER 3 — Add a lane-level test for scripts/modules/sd-next/display/quick-fixes.js: topStartableQF skips a QF whose id is in inFlightQfIds and selects the next eligible one, plus the TS-12 parity pair (absent Set and empty Set both change nothing). This lane currently has zero assertions.

BLOCKER 4 — Add the TS-12 parity test for the worker-checkin self-claim lane (scripts/worker-checkin.cjs:667): selfClaimQuickFix with and without the in-flight input, asserting an in-flight QF is skipped and behaviour is unchanged when the probe is UNAVAILABLE.

REQUIRED 5 — Eliminate the live gh/git calls from the unit tier. Give critical-qf-jump-inflight.test.js:83-86 an injected seam (it currently passes `{}`), and add an injection seam or an env guard to the worker-checkin.cjs:672 call so tests/unit/worker-checkin-qf-candidate-query-retry.test.js stops making a real network round-trip. A unit test whose verdict depends on live GitHub state is a latent flake.

REQUIRED 6 — Fix the batch repo derivation. Group candidates by target_application and probe per repo (the TTL cache is already keyed by repo, so this costs one extra call pair per distinct app), or withhold nothing for items whose target_application differs from the probed repo. Add a test with a mixed-target_application candidate list asserting no false CLEAR — this closes the gap TS-10 only half-covers.

RECOMMENDED 7 — Decouple the git probe from the default verdict: under includeBranchOnly=false, either skip `git ls-remote` entirely or do not let its failure force UNAVAILABLE, since branchRefs are discarded in that mode. Currently a git failure silently disables a PR-only guard, and the test at inflight-git-state.test.js:134-139 locks that in.

RECOMMENDED 8 — Record the default-change decision (PR-authoritative, branch-only opt-in) in the SD/PRD as a scope amendment with the 6-of-24 measurement, and note explicitly that the 6 were not partitioned into stale-merged vs active-WIP-without-PR. File the follow-on for branch-freshness filtering (exclude refs already merged into main by ancestry) so the push→open-PR window is eventually covered rather than silently dropped.
